issues.display_title: Issue #127: Backfill createdAt on the new accessPoints canvas array (FE #585)
issues.main_description_html:
The frontend shipped a new canvas object array, accessPoints (FE gothru-3d-floorplan#585, merged to development). StampCanvasCreatedAt does not know about it yet, so access markers never get the server-owned createdAt backfill every other object kind gets.

Background

Access (lifts and stairs) used to be an area — an AreaLayer whose type was "lift" or "stairs". It is now its own point object, stored per level as:

{
  "levels": [
    {
      "level_id": "L1",
      "accessPoints": [
        { "id": "a1", "x": 120, "y": 340, "accessId": "g1", "type": "lift",
          "name": "Main lift", "infoId": "i9", "createdAt": 1786... }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Storage needs no change — StampCanvasCreatedAt walks the blob as generic JSON (map[string]any), so the new key already round-trips untouched. That was verified while writing this; it is only the createdAt backfill that is missing.

The change

src/action/v1/shared/createdat.go — add one entry to canvasObjectPaths:

var canvasObjectPaths = [][]string{
	{"layout", "walls"},
	{"layout", "areas"},
	{"floorplanMeta", "doors"},
	{"floorplanMeta", "windows"},
	{"shapes"},
	{"points"},
	{"safetyAnnotations"},
	{"accessPoints"},   // <- new (FE #585)
	{"panoramas"},
}

That is the whole change. The file's own comment already anticipates it: "only a brand-new object ARRAY needs a line here."

Why it matters

createdAt is what orders the editor's object list newest-first (FE #392). An access marker that reaches the server without one keeps none, so it sorts as the oldest object forever — it sinks to the bottom of the list no matter when the user drew it.

That is not hypothetical: the frontend has a known bug where a marker placed right after a level loads is not stamped client-side (levelToModel hands the engine the store's own array by reference, so the object is already in prev when the stamp is decided). The server backfill is exactly the safety net for that case, which is why every other object array is listed.

Acceptance Criteria

  • {"accessPoints"} added to canvasObjectPaths
  • A level whose accessPoints[] objects have no createdAt comes back with each stamped 1 (unknownCreatedAt), matching the existing behaviour for points / safetyAnnotations
  • An existing createdAt on an access point is never overwritten
  • Unknown fields on an access point (accessId, type, name, infoId, accessOriginLevelId) still round-trip untouched
  • Test added in src/action/v1/shared/createdat_test.go alongside the existing per-array cases
  • go test ./... green

Assigned to: Pebi Sandi Pratama — Backend Developer

RESULT 10/08/26

✅ Implementation: Feedback Submission API (Task #123 / PR #134 )

Overview

This task adds POST /v1/feedback for authenticated users. The endpoint validates feedback, stores immutable user snapshots, and creates each record with status new.

Code Implementation

  1. Feedback Action (src/action/v1/feedback/create.go):

    • Parses required fields: area, category, rating, comment, path, and submitted_at.
    • Accepts optional project_id and project_name.
    • Accepts categories bug, confusing, missing, slow, and praise, matching the frontend contract.
    • Restricts ratings to values from 1 through 5.
    • Reads user ID, name, and email from middleware.GetUser(c); client-provided identity fields are ignored.
    • Persists the feedback using one DB.Create call.
    • Returns 201 with the generated feedback ID and status new.
    • Returns 400 for invalid payloads and 500 for persistence failures.

  2. Controller and Route:

    • Added the feedback controller under src/controllers/v1/feedback.
    • Registered POST /v1/feedback in src/routes/v1/feedback.go.
    • Applies middleware.Auth() only; SupportOnly() is intentionally not used because normal authenticated users submit feedback.
    • Registered feedback routes in src/routes/routes.go.

  3. API Collection (api-collection/v1/feedback):

    • Added the feedback folder and authenticated submission request.
    • Included a complete payload example and validation constraints.

Testing

Tests cover:

  • Successful submission with status new.
  • Authenticated user ID, name, and email snapshots.
  • Client-controlled user ID rejection.
  • Submission with and without project context.
  • Every missing required field returning 400.
  • Invalid category and rating returning 400.
  • Unauthenticated requests returning 401.
  • Isolated in-memory databases per test so shuffled execution cannot leak rows between tests.

issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 10/08/26

✅ Implementation: Support Feedback List and Detail API (Task #124)

Overview

This task adds the support inbox read API: a searchable, filterable, deterministically sorted feedback list and a complete feedback detail endpoint. Both routes require authentication and the exact global support role.

Endpoints

  • GET /v1/support/feedback
  • GET /v1/support/feedback/:id

The list deliberately lives under /v1/support/feedback, keeping all support routes behind one middleware group while /v1/feedback remains the authenticated user submission route.

Code Implementation

  1. Support Route Group (src/routes/v1/feedback.go):

    • Added a /support/feedback group protected by middleware.Auth() and middleware.SupportOnly().
    • Registered list and detail routes on that group.
    • Unauthenticated requests return 401; authenticated non-support users return 403.

  2. Feedback List (src/action/v1/feedback/read.go):

    • Supports search, status, category, area, project_id, and sort query parameters.
    • Validates statuses against new, reviewing, replied, resolved, and closed.
    • Validates sort modes against newest, oldest, recently_updated, and status.
    • Filters use fixed server-owned column names and bound query values.
    • Search matches comment, user email, project name, area, category, and path case-insensitively.
    • Escapes backslash, %, and _, preventing user input from becoming unintended SQL LIKE wildcards.
    • Preloads reply history in deterministic creation order.

  3. Deterministic Sorting (src/action/v1/feedback/read.go):

    • newest: creation time descending.
    • oldest: creation time ascending.
    • recently_updated: update time descending.
    • status: workflow order new, reviewing, replied, resolved, closed.
    • Every mode adds id ASC as a stable tie-breaker.

  4. Feedback Detail (src/action/v1/feedback/read.go):

    • Loads one complete feedback record by ID.
    • Includes full comment, user snapshots, optional project context, status, internal notes, timestamps, and reply history.
    • Returns 404 for an unknown ID and 500 for database failures.

  5. Response Contract (src/action/v1/feedback/read.go):

    • Uses a support-specific response type.
    • Exposes internal notes as notes, matching the support API contract.
    • List responses use data.feedback as an array; detail responses use data.feedback as one object.

  6. Controller and API Collection:

    • Added list and detail forwarding methods to the feedback controller.
    • Added API collection requests for both support endpoints.

Testing

src/action/v1/feedback/read_test.go covers:

  • Support user receives feedback records.
  • Status, category, area, and project filters.
  • Search across all six required fields.
  • Literal % and _ search behavior.
  • All four deterministic sort modes.
  • Workflow status order including closed.
  • Invalid status and sort values returning 400.

issues.display_title: Issue #131: Duplicate project: owner-only POST /v1/projects/:id/duplicate (row + files + blobs, copy is a draft)
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Add POST /v1/projects/:id/duplicate — an owner-only endpoint that forks a project into a fully independent copy.

  • Owner only. Stricter than publish/unpublish/delete (which accept role.CanWrite()): an editor member may change a project but may not fork it into a new project they would own. Non-owner → 403 via members.Forbidden(project).
  • Copy the row. Every column of projects is copied except: new id, freshly generated unique project_key, name = "{name} - copy", status = "draft", last_opened_at = NULL.
  • Never inherit publish state. Duplicating a published project must not publish the copy — the copy is a draft on a brand-new share key, so the original's /v/{key} link is untouched and the copy has no public link until its owner publishes it.
  • Copy the files. Every project_files row is recreated under the new project id and every stored blob is physically copied — both storage drivers (local disk under STORAGE_PATH/<projectId>/ and MinIO under the <projectId>/ object prefix). File names are kept identical, so every fileName reference inside the copied JSON blobs still resolves.
  • Re-point the JSON blobs. The frontend bakes the project id into stored file references — floor_configs[].serverPath (minio:///<projectId>/<file>) and the /api/files?projectId=<id>&name=… URLs inside information_records and generated_twins. Since file names are unchanged, swapping the source id for the new id inside floor_configs, generated_twins, canvas_data, information_records and categories re-points all of them. Everything else in those blobs is a nanoid, which never contains a project uuid.
  • Members / invitations are NOT copied. The duplicate belongs to the owner alone until they share it.
  • Failure after the row is created rolls the duplicate back (DeleteProject).

Why

There is no way to branch off an existing project today — the only path is rebuilding a floor plan from scratch. Users want to try changes, produce a variant of a venue, or keep a snapshot before a big edit, without touching the published original.

Doing this on the backend rather than orchestrating create + PATCH + re-upload from the frontend is the only way to copy the stored blobs at all: the FE has no list-files endpoint, and re-uploading would mint new file names and break every reference in the JSON.

Acceptance Criteria

  • POST /v1/projects/:id/duplicate returns 201 with the standard project response for the copy
  • Only the owner may call it — an editor member gets 403 with the owner-naming body, and no copy is created
  • Unknown id → 404; unauthenticated → 401
  • Copy has a new id, a new unique project_key, name = "{original} - copy", status = "draft" — including when the original is published
  • All content columns are copied: canvas_data, floor_configs, generated_twins, information_records, categories, active_level_id, canvas_filter, map_style, floor_image_opacity, description, location_*, is_complete
  • Every project_files row is recreated for the copy, with file_url re-pointed at the new project id
  • Every stored blob is physically copied under the new project id, on both the local-disk and MinIO drivers
  • Stored file paths inside the copied blobs point at the copy, not the original
  • Editing the copy (row, blobs or files) leaves the original completely untouched, and vice versa
  • Build + tests green

Dependencies

None. FE counterpart (dashboard "Duplicate" menu item + duplicateProject server action) ships on gothru-3d-floormap and depends on this endpoint.

RESULT

Implemented on feature/131-duplicate-project, commit 30a009e, merged to development via PR #132 (f739d7c).

Files

  • src/action/v1/project/duplicate.go (new) — Duplicate handler, copyProjectFiles, copyProjectBlob, repointProjectBlobs
  • src/controllers/v1/project/duplicate.go (new)
  • src/routes/v1/projects.go — projects.Post("/:id/duplicate", pc.Duplicate)
  • src/action/v1/project/duplicate_test.go (new)

How it works

  • Loads the project, resolves the caller's role with members.FetchRoleForProject, and rejects anything but RoleOwner with members.Forbidden(project) — stricter than publish/delete's CanWrite(), so an editor member cannot fork a project.
  • Copies the row struct wholesale, then resets Base, ProjectKey, Files, sets name = "{name} - copy", status = "draft", last_opened_at = NULL, and creates it through the existing createProjectWithGeneratedKey retry helper so the copy gets its own unique share key.
  • copyProjectFiles recreates every project_files row under the new id with file_url re-pointed, and copyProjectBlob physically copies each blob — ReadObject/PutObject for MinIO, io.Copy into STORAGE_PATH/<newId>/ for local disk — keeping identical file names so all fileName references stay valid.
  • repointProjectBlobs swaps the source id for the new id inside floor_configs, generated_twins, canvas_data, information_records and categories, which covers the two places the FE bakes the project id into stored references: floor_configs[].serverPath (minio:///<projectId>/<file>) and the /api/files?projectId=<id>&name= URLs in information records. Exact because file names are unchanged; every other id in those blobs is a nanoid.
  • Any failure after the row exists rolls the duplicate back with DeleteProject.
  • Members and invitations are deliberately not copied — the duplicate belongs to the owner alone until they share it.

Tests

  • TestDuplicateCopiesEverythingAsADraft — a published original yields a - copy draft with a new key, the blob and file row are copied, serverPath is re-pointed at the new id, and editing the copy (row + blob) leaves the original untouched.
  • TestDuplicateIsOwnerOnly — an editor member gets 403 and no second project row is created.

✅ Implementation: Support Feedback Reply ( Task #126 / PR #138 )

Summary

Implemented issue #126: authenticated support users can reply to feedback by email through Plunk. A reply is added to history only after email delivery succeeds, then the feedback status changes to replied.

Endpoint

Authorization: Bearer <support-token>

{

RESULT 11/08/26

✅ Implementation: Support Feedback Pagination ( Task #136 / PR #139 )

Summary

Implemented issue #136 in PR #139: GET /v1/support/feedback now returns a bounded page instead of every matching feedback row. The existing data.feedback array remains unchanged, with pagination metadata added beside it.

API

GET /v1/support/feedback?page=1&per_page=20
Authorization: Bearer <support-token>

Pagination composes with all existing list parameters:

  • search
  • status
  • category
  • area
  • project_id
  • sort
  • page
  • per_page

Defaults and Validation

  • Default page: 1
  • Default per_page: 20
  • Maximum per_page: 100
  • Either parameter may be omitted independently.
  • Non-numeric, zero, negative, or over-limit values return 400.
  • Page values that would overflow the SQL offset calculation also return 400.
  • A page after the final result returns 200 with an empty feedback array.

Response

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "requestTime": 1,
  "data": {
    "feedback": [],
    "total": 0,
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 20
  }
}

total counts every row matching the active filters before LIMIT and OFFSET are applied.

Query Behavior

The same filtered GORM query is used for the total count and paginated rows. Existing deterministic ordering remains intact because every sort mode retains id ASC as its final tie-breaker. This prevents duplicates or missing rows while traversing a fixed dataset page by page.

Reply history is no longer preloaded by the list endpoint. Full ordered history remains available from GET /v1/support/feedback/:id. This reduces list query work and response size.

issues.display_title: Issue #141: Stripe webhook signing secret is logged in plaintext on signature failure
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 11/08/26

✅ Implementation: Stripe Webhook Secret Redaction

Summary

Implemented issue #141 in PR #143. Invalid Stripe webhook signatures no longer cause STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET to be written to application logs.

The webhook remains public and continues to authenticate Stripe callbacks through the Stripe-Signature header. Only diagnostic logging changed; event verification and billing behavior remain unchanged.

Security Issue

The previous invalid-signature log rendered the signing secret with %q:

log.Printf("... Secret: %q ...", secret)

Anyone could trigger this path by sending an invalid signature to:

POST /v1/billing/webhook

Users with access to pm2 output, container logs, or log shipping could then read the secret and forge Stripe webhook signatures.

Fix

The log now records only the secret length:

log.Printf(
    "WEBHOOK ERROR - Body Len: %d | Signature Len: %d | Secret Len: %d | Error: %v\n",
    len(body), len(signature), len(secret), err,
)

The length preserves a useful presence/configuration signal without exposing secret material. Webhook validation failures still return 400.

Files Changed

  • src/action/v1/billing/webhook.go
  • src/action/v1/billing/webhook_test.go

No route, model, database, environment-file, or migration changes were required.

Regression Test

TestWebhookInvalidSignatureDoesNotLogSigningSecret:

  1. Sets a known STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
  2. Captures the standard logger output.
  3. Sends a webhook request with an invalid signature.
  4. Verifies the response is 400.
  5. Verifies the raw signing secret is absent from logs.
  6. Verifies the log contains only Secret Len: 31 for the test value.
  7. Restores the process-wide logger configuration during cleanup.

Secret Log Audit

Go log call sites were audited against these secret environment names:

  • STRIPE_*
  • USEPLUNK_SECRET_KEY
  • JWT_SECRET
  • MINIO_SECRET_KEY

No other log statement was found printing these secrets.

Verification

Commands used:

go test ./src/action/v1/billing -run TestWebhookInvalidSignatureDoesNotLogSigningSecret -count=1
go test ./src/action/v1/billing -count=1
go build ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

The focused regression test, billing package tests, build, vet, and diff check passed. The repository-wide test suite still had the unrelated existing TestPredictStreamsSSEEvents failure: its test expects /predict/txt, while current production code calls /txt.

Required Operational Action

The old signing secret must be treated as compromised because it may remain in retained logs. Merging the code fix prevents future exposure but does not invalidate previously leaked values.

After deploying PR #143:

  1. Rotate the webhook signing secret in Stripe Dashboard.
  2. Replace STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in every deployed environment.
  3. Restart the API processes so they load the new value.
  4. Send a Stripe test webhook and confirm signature verification succeeds.
  5. Revoke or remove the previous secret after the new configuration is verified.

Do not write either old or new secret into repository files, issue comments, PR comments, or logs.

Pre-existing, unrelated to the feedback series — found while reviewing #139.

Description

src/action/v1/billing/webhook.go:32 writes the Stripe webhook signing secret to stdout in plaintext every time signature verification fails:

log.Printf("WEBHOOK ERROR - Body Len: %d | Signature Len: %d | Secret: %q | Error: %v\n",
    len(body), len(signature), secret, err)

secret is os.Getenv("STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET") (line 27), rendered raw with %q. Note the line is otherwise careful — body and signature are logged as lengths precisely so their contents do not leak — so the secret is the one value that was meant to be described and instead gets printed.

POST /v1/billing/webhook is public (src/routes/v1/billing.go:16, no middleware.Auth()), so anyone who can reach the endpoint can trigger the log line at will by posting a body with a bad signature.

Anyone with log access — the pm2 output, the container logs, or any shipper they are forwarded to — can read the signing secret and forge webhook events that the API will accept as genuine Stripe callbacks. Billing state is driven by those events (customer.subscription.created, customer.subscription.updated), so a forged event can change a subscription.

This also conflicts with the documented convention in src/config/database.go:51, where query parameters are suppressed from logs with the comment "Jangan log parameter (seperti email) untuk alasan keamanan".

Acceptance Criteria

  • The signing secret is no longer written to logs — log its length if a presence check is useful, consistent with how body and signature are handled on the same line
  • No other log statement in the repo prints a secret; grep for STRIPE_, USEPLUNK_SECRET_KEY, JWT_SECRET, and MINIO_SECRET_KEY against log. call sites
  • STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET rotated in the Stripe dashboard and in the deployed environment after the fix ships — the current value must be assumed compromised, since it may already sit in retained logs
  • Test: a webhook request with an invalid signature still returns 400 and the emitted log line contains no secret material

RESULT 11/08/26

✅ Implementation: Feedback API Collection Fixes ( Task #140 / PR #142 )

Summary

Implemented issue #140 in PR #142. The Bruno feedback collection now uses the environment's bearer token, provides reusable feedback IDs, points the DEV environment at the deployed API, and documents the current /v1/auth/me response.

This change affects collection documentation and test configuration only. API behavior, routes, models, and database schema remain unchanged.

Authentication Fix

The Feedback folder previously inherited this nonexistent variable:

token: "{{token}}"

It now uses the collection-wide convention:

token: "{{bearerToken}}"

All five feedback requests inherit this folder authentication:

  • Submit feedback
  • List support feedback
  • Get support feedback
  • Update support feedback
  • Reply to support feedback

Setting bearerToken once in the selected Bruno environment therefore authenticates every feedback request.

Environment Variables

Both environments now define:

- name: feedbackId
  value: <FEEDBACK_ID>

The value is consumed by the feedback detail, update, and reply requests. Testers can paste one created feedback ID into the environment instead of editing three request URLs.

DEV.yml also now defines:

- name: baseUrl
  value: http://192.168.1.226:7070
- name: bearerToken
  value: <YOUR_JWT_TOKEN>

Local - Dev.yml keeps http://127.0.0.1:7070 and its existing bearerToken placeholder.

Current User Example

The successful /v1/auth/me examples now include:

{
  "role": "support",
  "has_password": true
}

The obsolete example content-length header was removed because adding response fields makes the old fixed length incorrect. Endpoint documentation now mentions role and password availability.

  • api-collection/environments/DEV.yml
  • api-collection/environments/Local - Dev.yml

  2. Select DEV or Local - Dev.
  3. Replace <YOUR_JWT_TOKEN> with a valid token for a user whose global role is support.
  4. Run Submit feedback or use an existing feedback record.
  5. Replace <FEEDBACK_ID> with that feedback ID.
  6. Run all five feedback requests and Get current user.

  • Get current user returns role and has_password.

Verification

  • git diff --check passes.

auth:
  type: bearer

No environment defines token. environments/Local - Dev.yml and environments/DEV.yml define only baseUrl, bearerToken, and googleIdToken. Counting across the whole collection: {{bearerToken}} appears 31 times, {{token}} appears once — here.

All five feedback requests declare auth: inherit, so every one of them sends an empty bearer and gets 401, even when the tester has pasted a valid token into the environment. The endpoints themselves are fine; this was verified live against the deployed API with a real support token, where all five respond correctly.

Feedback is also the only folder in the collection that declares its own auth: block. Every other folder leaves auth to the individual request, e.g. api-collection/v1/auth/me/Get current user.yml:

  auth:
    type: bearer
    token: "{{bearerToken}}"

Introduced in 63449c8 and inherited by each later feedback PR.

2. {{feedbackId}} is never defined. It is used by Get support feedback.yml, Update support feedback.yml, and Reply to support feedback.yml, but appears in neither environment, so those three requests cannot be run without editing the URL by hand.

3. No environment points at a reachable server. Three different values, none of them the dev API at 192.168.1.226:7070:

File baseUrl

environments/DEV.yml http://<SERVER_IP>:9999 — literal placeholder, and the port is wrong
environments/Local - Dev.yml http://127.0.0.1:7070

  • All five feedback requests return something other than 401 when a valid support token is set in the environment

issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 11/08/26

✅ Implementation: Support Feedback Multi-Status Filter

Summary

Implemented issue #144. GET /v1/support/feedback now accepts multiple comma-separated status values, allowing the support dashboard to request complete solved or unsolved result sets before pagination.

Existing single-status requests remain compatible.

API Usage

Solved feedback:

GET /v1/support/feedback?status=resolved,closed

Unsolved feedback:

GET /v1/support/feedback?status=new,reviewing,replied

Single-status filtering still works:

GET /v1/support/feedback?status=reviewing

The parameter composes with existing search, category, area, project, sorting, and pagination parameters.

Validation

The endpoint:

  1. Splits status on commas.
  2. Trims whitespace around every value.
  3. Validates every value against the existing status set:
    • new
    • reviewing
    • replied
    • resolved
    • closed
  4. Returns 400 when any value is empty or invalid.

Examples returning 400:

status=invalid
status=resolved,invalid
status=resolved,,closed

Query Behavior

Validated status values are applied through a parameterized GORM query:

query.Where("status IN ?", statuses)

The filtered query is used for both:

  • total count calculation
  • Paginated feedback retrieval

This ensures the pager and dashboard totals represent the complete solved or unsolved dataset instead of only the current page.

Files Changed

  • src/action/v1/feedback/read.go
  • src/action/v1/feedback/read_test.go
  • api-collection/v1/feedback/List support feedback.yml

No route, model, database, or migration changes were required.

Tests

Coverage includes:

  • Exact solved membership: resolved and closed.
  • Exact unsolved membership: new, reviewing, and replied.
  • Correct total for both grouped filters.
  • Existing single-status compatibility.
  • Whitespace trimming around CSV values.
  • Invalid single values.
  • Mixed valid and invalid values.
  • Empty values inside a comma-separated list.

API Collection

The Bruno list request documents the comma-separated status format and includes the unsolved example:

status=new,reviewing,replied

Its documentation also identifies:

  • Solved: resolved,closed
  • Unsolved: new,reviewing,replied

Verification

Commands used:

go test ./src/action/v1/feedback -count=1
go build ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

The feedback tests, build, vet, and diff check passed. The repository-wide suite still has the unrelated existing TestPredictStreamsSSEEvents failure: its test expects /predict/txt, while current production code calls /txt.

Raised while implementing the frontend list alignment (GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#584). Follow-up to #124 and #136.

Description

The support dashboard's primary control is a Solved / Unsolved / All filter. It cannot be expressed as a request today, so it runs client-side over whatever page the frontend happens to be holding — which, since pagination shipped in #136, means it narrows the current page only. Ask for "unsolved" on a table of 500 and you get the unsolved rows out of the 20 in hand, not the unsolved rows overall.

The gap is that "solved" is two statuses, not one:

// frontend: src/app/support/SupportDashboardClient.tsx
function isSolved(status) { return status === "resolved" || status === "closed" }

while GET /v1/support/feedback takes a single value:

// src/action/v1/feedback/read.go
query = query.Where("status = ?", value)

so ?status=resolved misses closed, and there is no way to ask for "either". The same is true in reverse for unsolved, which is new, reviewing, and replied together.

The counts are affected as well: the dashboard header shows a solved/unsolved split that is page-scoped for the same reason. The frontend currently labels that pair "on this page" so the numbers do not claim to be global, but that is a description of the limitation, not a fix.

Options

Either would work; the first is smaller and composes with the existing validation.

  1. Let status accept a comma-separated list — ?status=resolved,closed — validating each value against validStatuses and using IN (?). Existing single-value callers keep working unchanged.
  2. Add a dedicated ?solved=true|false parameter that maps to the two groupings server-side.

Whichever is chosen, total must reflect the same filter so the frontend pager stays correct.

Acceptance Criteria

  • The list endpoint can return exactly the solved set (resolved + closed) or the unsolved set (new + reviewing + replied) in one request
  • Invalid values still produce 400, consistent with the current status validation
  • total respects the new filter, so pagination stays correct
  • Existing single-value ?status= requests keep working
  • Tests: solved set, unsolved set, invalid value → 400, and total correct under the new filter
  • api-collection/v1/feedback/List support feedback.yml documents the parameter

Frontend counterpart

Once this ships, the solved filter moves into the request and the header counts can be sourced from the server instead of the page. Tracked against gothru-3d-floormap#584.

  • An unrecognised DB_DRIVER fails at startup with a clear message instead of guessing.
  • README: state that Postgres is the default and the only supported driver.

issues.display_title: Issue #153: Mappedin import returns floors in the export's arbitrary order — sort each floor stack by floors.geojson elevation (and carry the stacks as buildings)
issues.main_description_html:
Backend counterpart to the frontend fix in GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#673 (report: #628). The Go parser and the TypeScript parser read the same Mappedin export and now disagree about what comes out of it.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
File: src/utils/mappedin.go · Endpoint: POST /v1/import/mappedin (src/routes/v1/import.go:14)
FE reference implementation: src/lib/mappedin/parse.ts on development (merged as 7256f20)

Why now

A Mappedin export does not list its floors in physical order. The asset from the report — Multi-Family Hi-Rise Demo, 36 floors, one floor stack — lists them as:

Level 1, Mezzanine, Level 2, Level 3, Level 4, RA, Level 24, Level 17, Level 8, Level 19, Level 33, …

Neither ascending nor descending. The real order is floors.geojson elevation: per the MVF v3 spec it is required, an integer ordinal, 0 = ground, negatives below grade, and unique within a floor stack rather than within the file. Mappedin's own Web SDK sorts its level selector by it. Sorting that 36-floor stack ascending yields Level 1, Mezzanine, Level 2 … Level 34, PH, RA, which is what the reference viewer shows.

The FE now does this. The Go parser does not, so the two return different level orders for identical input.

Part 1 — floor order (must)

src/utils/mappedin.go:347-358 appends the stack verbatim and never sorts:

var floorIDs []string
floorStacks, err := readJSONFromZip[[]FloorStackEntry](files, "floor-stacks.json")
if err == nil && floorStacks != nil {
    for _, stack := range *floorStacks {
        floorIDs = append(floorIDs, stack.Floors...)   // ← file order, unsorted
    }
}

grep -i elevation src/**/*.go returns nothing — FloorsGeoJson (:235-244) reads only id, maxHeight, details.name.

Note the Go side does not even reverse, so one file currently has three possible orders across the stack: Go returns raw file order, the pre-fix FE returned it reversed, the fixed FE returns it sorted. Only the third is correct.

Change: read elevation into the struct, sort each stack by it ascending (sort.SliceStable), and keep the feature's own index in floors.geojson as the fallback when elevation is absent — not 0, which would drop an unannotated floor next to the ground floor. Ascending matches canvasData.levels bottom→top, the same contract the FE holds.

Sort per stack, not over the flattened list: elevation is unique only inside one stack, so a global sort interleaves buildings.

Part 2 — building grouping (should)

Same twelve lines, same reason it is worth doing together. FloorStackEntry (:247-249) is:

type FloorStackEntry struct {
    Floors []string `json:"floors"`
}

No id, no details.name, and every stack is flattened into one floorIDs. MappedinConvertResult (:71-75) has no Buildings, and LevelData carries no BuildingID.

A Mappedin floor stack is a building. The FE established that in gothru-3d-floormap#643 and shipped it through the whole wizard in #662: each stack becomes its own building record and every level is stamped with its own building id. A multi-building export through this endpoint currently collapses into one building.

Change: carry id and details.name on FloorStackEntry, return a buildings array, and stamp each level with its own building id — matching ParsedBuilding / CanvasData.buildings in the FE.

Reasonable to split into its own issue if Part 1 needs to ship alone; they are named together because they are the same function and the same read of floor-stacks.json.

Blast radius

Nothing regresses today. The FE proxy routes (src/app/api/import/mappedin/route.ts, .../mappedin-editor/route.ts) are not called from anywhere in src/ — import runs client-side. This is a contract-alignment task, not a live bug. src/lib/mappedin-import/detectSource.ts:10 already carries a note that the two parsers must be reconciled.

/v1/import/mappedin-editor (the .txt editor export) is not affected: that format carries no floor or elevation signal at all.

Acceptance

  • POST /v1/import/mappedin returns floors bottom→top by elevation, per floor stack.
  • An export with no elevation keeps its floors.geojson order rather than collapsing to the ground floor.
  • Negative elevations sort correctly (Airport Demo: Level 1 = −1 below Level 2 = 0).
  • Floors of a multi-stack export stay contiguous per stack; no interleaving.
  • (Part 2) The response carries buildings, one per floor stack, and every level is stamped with its own building id.
  • Go tests cover the scrambled 36-floor order and the colliding-elevation two-stack case.
  • The endpoint's output matches parse.ts for the same zip.

Verification

The 36-floor asset is attached to gothru-3d-floormap#628 and lives at .playwright-mcp/demo/628/mappedin-hi-rise-36-floors.zip in the FE repo. Expected order out:

Level 1, Mezzanine, Level 2 … Level 12, Level 14 … Level 34, PH, RA

(there is no "Level 13" in the building — elevation runs 0..35 dense over 36 floors)

RESULT

Branch: fix/153-mappedin-floor-order · Commit: 4bfd757 · PR: #154, merged into development as 5c0ee48 · 2 files, +470/−19

Both parts landed together — same function, same read of floor-stacks.json.

Part 1 — floor order

src/utils/mappedin.go now builds a sort key per floor from floors.geojson elevation and orders each stack by its own, ascending — bottom→top, matching canvasData.levels.

  • Per stack, never across the file: elevation is unique only inside one stack, so a global sort interleaves two buildings that both number from 0.
  • Fallback is the feature's own index in floors.geojson, not 0 — 0 would strand an unannotated floor beside the ground floor. NaN/Inf are guarded, since a comparator returning NaN gives sort arbitrary order.

Part 2 — floor stacks are buildings

FloorStackEntry carries the stack's id and details.name. canvasData gained buildings, and every level and floor is stamped with its own buildingId.

JSON matches the frontend shape exactly: {id, name, imported} plus buildingId on levels and floors, all omitempty. The imported flag is load-bearing — the frontend finds the user's own manual building by the absence of it, never by name, so an unflagged import would swallow the user's uploads. Building id is the stack's own id from the file, mirroring ParsedBuilding in the frontend's parse.ts; a stack whose floors all failed to load is dropped rather than shipped empty.

Verification

The real 36-floor asset through this parser:

FLOORS (36): Level 1 | Mezzanine | Level 2 | … | Level 34 | PH | RA
BUILDING id=fs_67a6641530e940000bac3c1a name="Multi-Family Hi-Rise Demo" imported=true
levels=36 stamped=36

Identical to what the frontend produces for the same file, so the two parsers agree again.

Eight tests in src/utils/mappedin_test.go over an in-memory export builder: the real 36-floor order, the floors.geojson fallback with no floor-stacks.json, two stacks with colliding 0..2 elevations, an export with no elevation, negative elevations (Airport Demo), building metadata, the positional Building N fallback, and the single-venue case.

The four ordering tests were confirmed to fail with the sort disabled — they catch the defect rather than passing by luck.

go build ./... OK · gofmt -l clean · go vet clean · go test ./src/utils/ ok

Not from this change

TestPredictStreamsSSEEvents (src/action/v1/predict) fails on development before this branch — verified by reverting these two files and re-running. Inference API path /txt vs /predict/txt; unrelated and untouched. Needs its own issue.

issues.main_description_html:
Backend counterpart to GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#250 (PR gothru-3d-floormap#776). The share card for a published project has no image it can point at: every file the FE can upload is behind middleware.Auth(), and a crawler never carries a token.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
Files: src/routes/v1/floorplan.go · src/controllers/v1/files/ · src/action/v1/shared/object_storage.go
FE reference: src/app/v/[key]/layout.tsx + src/lib/preview/ogImage.ts on branch feature/250-share-meta-card

Why now

/v/{key} now emits a server-rendered Open Graph card. The image half of it has nowhere to read from:

request result
GET /v1/projects/{id}/file?name=… without a Bearer 401 — the whole projects group is middleware.Auth() (src/routes/v1/projects.go:14)
GET /v1/files?name=… 404, identical to a nonexistent path — the route is not registered

/v1/files is dead code. src/controllers/v1/files/get.go and src/action/v1/files/get.go exist, but nothing in src/routes/** ever wires them: grep -rn 'files.Get' src/routes/ is empty and so is git log -S'files.Get' -- src/routes/, so this handler has never been reachable.

Even if it were wired it would not answer this need. It resolves through CheckSession + ObjectKey(session, filename) → {session}/{filename} (src/action/v1/shared/object_storage.go:40), while POST /v1/projects/:id/file stores under {projectID}/{filename}. Different prefix, so a project file can never be found by name alone.

The FE PR assumed the bare ?name= branch was a working anonymous read and shipped an upload against it. Until this task lands, that upload writes a JPEG nobody can fetch and every share card falls back to the static site image.

Proposal A (recommended) — public, published-only file read by share key

GET /v1/live/:key/file?name=<basename>
  • Resolve the project by project_key, exactly like GET /v1/live/:key (src/routes/v1/floorplan.go:15, task #85).
  • Serve only when status = 'published'. Draft → 404, unknown key → 404, missing object → 404, all with an identical body so the endpoint leaks nothing about which projects exist.
  • Read {project.ID}/{name} through the existing ReadObject; keep ObjectKey's validation (basename only, no dotfiles, no separators) so name cannot escape the project prefix.

issues.main_description_html:
Follow-up to #159. Backend counterpart to GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#250 (PR #776).

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
File: src/action/v1/files/project_upload.go · Endpoint: POST /v1/projects/:id/file

Why now

#159 shipped GET /v1/live/:key/file?name= so a crawler can read a published project's share-card image. The read works. The write cannot produce a name the reader can ask for:

fileExt := strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(fileHeader.Filename))
uniqueFileName := fmt.Sprintf("%s%s", uuid.NewString(), fileExt)   // src/action/v1/files/project_upload.go:74

Every upload is renamed to a fresh UUID, and that name is what goes into the object key, the disk path, and project_files.file_name. So the frontend uploads og.jpg and the object is stored as 9f3c….jpg; ?name=og.jpg then finds no row and 404s.

The name is only discoverable from the upload response, which the crawler never sees — and the screenshot is deliberately not persisted anywhere in the project blob. A caller has to be able to say what the object is called.

Change

Accept an optional name form field on POST /v1/projects/:id/file:

  • Absent → current behaviour exactly: a generated UUID name. No existing upload path changes.
  • Present → validate and use it as the stored name. It must be a bare basename (no separators, no leading dot) and its extension must match the uploaded file's, so a JPEG cannot be stored under an .html name.
  • Re-uploading the same name overwrites in place — object and row both — rather than piling up rows the readers would have to disambiguate. That is exactly what republishing a project should do to its share card.

Write access is already gated (role.CanWrite()), so the only thing a named upload can overwrite is a file in a project the caller may already write to.

Acceptance Criteria

  • POST /v1/projects/{id}/file with name=og.jpg stores the object as {projectID}/og.jpg and a project_files row with file_name = "og.jpg"
  • GET /v1/live/{key}/file?name=og.jpg then returns those bytes for a published project (the #159 path, end to end)
  • Uploading og.jpg twice leaves one row and the newer bytes
  • name with a separator, a leading dot, or an extension that disagrees with the file → 400, nothing written
  • Omitting name still yields a UUID name — existing floor plan / photo uploads are untouched

Not in scope

The public viewer's Information and Event photos are stored as fully-formed /api/files?projectId=… URLs and hit the 401 branch for anonymous visitors. Those names are known (they carry the generated UUID), so #159 already covers them from the backend side — the fix is a frontend one and belongs in its own issue.

issues.display_title: Issue #168: Project visibility: is_public column, PATCH key, and the three public read gates
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Add POST /v1/projects/:id/duplicate — an owner-only endpoint that forks a project into a fully independent copy.

  • Owner only. Stricter than publish/unpublish/delete (which accept role.CanWrite()): an editor member may change a project but may not fork it into a new project they would own. Non-owner → 403 via members.Forbidden(project).
  • Copy the row. Every column of projects is copied except: new id, freshly generated unique project_key, name = "{name} - copy", status = "draft", last_opened_at = NULL.
  • Never inherit publish state. Duplicating a published project must not publish the copy — the copy is a draft on a brand-new share key, so the original's /v/{key} link is untouched and the copy has no public link until its owner publishes it.
  • Copy the files. Every project_files row is recreated under the new project id and every stored blob is physically copied — both storage drivers (local disk under STORAGE_PATH/<projectId>/ and MinIO under the <projectId>/ object prefix). File names are kept identical, so every fileName reference inside the copied JSON blobs still resolves.
  • Re-point the JSON blobs. The frontend bakes the project id into stored file references — floor_configs[].serverPath (minio:///<projectId>/<file>) and the /api/files?projectId=<id>&name=… URLs inside information_records and generated_twins. Since file names are unchanged, swapping the source id for the new id inside floor_configs, generated_twins, canvas_data, information_records and categories re-points all of them. Everything else in those blobs is a nanoid, which never contains a project uuid.
  • Members / invitations are NOT copied. The duplicate belongs to the owner alone until they share it.
  • Failure after the row is created rolls the duplicate back (DeleteProject).

Why

There is no way to branch off an existing project today — the only path is rebuilding a floor plan from scratch. Users want to try changes, produce a variant of a venue, or keep a snapshot before a big edit, without touching the published original.

Doing this on the backend rather than orchestrating create + PATCH + re-upload from the frontend is the only way to copy the stored blobs at all: the FE has no list-files endpoint, and re-uploading would mint new file names and break every reference in the JSON.

Acceptance Criteria

  • POST /v1/projects/:id/duplicate returns 201 with the standard project response for the copy
  • Only the owner may call it — an editor member gets 403 with the owner-naming body, and no copy is created
  • Unknown id → 404; unauthenticated → 401
  • Copy has a new id, a new unique project_key, name = "{original} - copy", status = "draft" — including when the original is published
  • All content columns are copied: canvas_data, floor_configs, generated_twins, information_records, categories, active_level_id, canvas_filter, map_style, floor_image_opacity, description, location_*, is_complete
  • Every project_files row is recreated for the copy, with file_url re-pointed at the new project id
  • Every stored blob is physically copied under the new project id, on both the local-disk and MinIO drivers
  • Stored file paths inside the copied blobs point at the copy, not the original
  • Editing the copy (row, blobs or files) leaves the original completely untouched, and vice versa
  • Build + tests green

Dependencies

None. FE counterpart (dashboard "Duplicate" menu item + duplicateProject server action) ships on gothru-3d-floormap and depends on this endpoint.

RESULT

PR #169 → development (4a0ea05), release PR #170 → main (2c86560). Work commit 21ca403. 8 files, +216 / −6.

Shipped — Project.IsPublic with gorm:"not null;default:true", so every project that predates the column stays exactly as reachable as it was. isPublic added to the PATCH /v1/projects/:id whitelist beside isComplete; it is untouched by the status guard at update.go:59, which is scoped to that one key. is_public serialized on projectResponse, so get/list/recent/update all carry it.

The three gates — /v1/live/:key answers 403 {"error":"project is private"}, the only endpoint that distinguishes private from missing, because the frontend has to say so. /v1/live/:key/file gained an is_public predicate and rejoins the shared 404, byte-identical to every other miss. /v1/floorplan/:id widened its condition to status != "published" || !IsPublic, so a private project falls back to the optional-auth member check — owner, editor and viewer keep it, a guest gets the same 404 a draft has always returned.

Migration — migrations/202609070001_add_is_public_to_projects.sql. Applied to the database ahead of the release, deliberately: without the column, SELECT * leaves IsPublic false for every row, so /v1/live/:key would have answered 403 to everyone and live_get.go would have thrown a SQL error. Verified after applying: 515 projects, all is_public = true.

Verified — src/routes/v1/project_visibility_test.go, 6 cases. Red-first: with src/action/ stashed, 4 of the 6 fail; restored, go build ./... and go test ./... green. issues.main_description_html:
Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

FE PRD: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#946 · Decisions: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#955
Depends on the schema task.

The actual gate: a secured project's content must never leave the API without proof of access.

There are THREE public read paths, not one

A gate on the route the ticket names would be bypassable on day one:

Route Returns Today
GET /v1/live/:key the whole floorplan is_public checked after load → 403
GET /v1/live/:key/file project files by name is_public folded into the WHERE → shared 404
GET /v1/floorplan/:id the identical payload, by UUID optional-auth member check

/v1/floorplan/:id is route-public and the UUID sits in the editor URL and in the browser's localStorage (gf_project_id). Put the gate where all three converge — buildFloorplanResponse in src/action/v1/floorplan/shared.go is that point — not on live.go alone.

Unlock endpoint

A public POST that takes the key and a password, verifies with utils.CheckPassword, and on success issues a project-scoped grant (see D4). It must not reveal whether the key exists differently from how /v1/live/:key already does.

Then every content read accepts that grant and refuses without it.

Object storage escapes the gate entirely

When MinIO is on, buildFloorplanResponse rewrites every fileUrl to a MinIO URL. With MINIO_PUBLIC_READ that is a permanently public bucket URL that does not pass through this API at all. The gate is worthless if those URLs are emitted before unlock — do not include them in a pre-unlock response.

Rate limiting

There is none in this repo (zero hits for limiter/ratelimit). Whatever D3 rules, implement it here — an anonymous unlock route with unlimited attempts against a no-complexity-rules password is a guessing oracle, and repeated bcrypt is also a CPU-exhaustion surface.

Tests

src/routes/v1/project_visibility_test.go and live_file_test.go are the pattern. Cover: locked project returns no content on all three routes; correct password issues a grant; wrong password does not; a grant for project A does not open project B; an expired/garbage grant is refused; unsecured and private projects behave exactly as before.

Blocked on

D2 (does a metadata-only response exist before unlock), D3 (throttling), D4 (what the grant is), D5 (is /file gated).

RESULT

Implemented on feature/172-secured-read-gate, merged in #174, released in #175 and deployed.

The gate lands on all three route-public reads. GET /v1/floorplan/:id returns the identical payload by UUID, and that UUID is published inside the live response's own uploadedFiles[].fileUrl — gating only /v1/live/:key would have left the password decorative. It answers for a secured project exactly as for a private one, and deliberately does not accept a grant.

GET /v1/live/:key answers 401 with the project name and nothing else. GET /v1/live/:key/file does take a grant, because an unlocked visitor still needs the floor images; without one it rejoins the shared 404, so it stays useless for enumeration.

VerifySessionToken now rejects any token carrying a grant type claim. Without that, a grant whose sub matched a real users.unique_id would have been accepted by middleware.Auth() as a 30-day login, and a stolen session token would have opened every secured project. Both directions are pinned by tests — the check was verified by breaking it and watching the test fail.

POST /v1/live/:key/unlock is rate limited per IP and project with the limiter already in the pinned Fiber module (no new dependency). R12 promises nobody is locked out; a rate satisfies that, an unmetered bcrypt oracle does not.

GET /v1/projects/:id/embed-grant mints the embed credential: same primitive, no expiry, deterministic per project so a link already placed in a customer's tour survives a password change. No revocation — rotating a leaked link needs a version counter on the project row; marked in the code.

Verified in production: map-thru.com/v/<key> on a secured project emits the project's own name in og:title (only the locked branch does that; private strips the name) and carries no canvasData.

Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Reported: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#935 · FE counterpart: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#972

Event Highlights carry a per-record draft flag now. This is the half that makes the flag mean anything — without it the frontend filter is decoration, because the draft still travels in the anonymous payload.

Build

  • stripDraftEvents(response) in src/action/v1/floorplan/shared.go. Filters the response, not the stored column, so the editor's own read still returns every draft.
  • live.go calls it unconditionally — every reader of /v1/live/:key is a visitor.
  • get.go calls it when the caller resolves to RoleNone. That route serves guests whenever the project is published and IsGuestReadable(), which makes it a second door onto the same content.

The rule is published !== false. Only an explicit false is dropped: an Event without the field predates the flag and was already public, so reading absence as a draft would empty the Event panel of every live map on deploy. The frontend applies the identical rule and the two were checked to agree on every JSON value the field can hold.

Not a schema change

The flag rides the existing event_records TEXT column. No migration, nothing to ALTER before or after.

Tests

src/action/v1/floorplan/draft_events_test.go — anonymous, signed-in stranger, viewer, owner, and the /v1/live/:key path. The two "keeps drafts" cases guard against over-stripping.

RESULT

Implemented on feature/935-event-publish-toggle, merged in #176, released in #177 and deployed.

get.go needed a small restructure, not just a call. Membership was resolved inside the access gate, but a published and guest-readable project skips that gate entirely — so an owner reading their own published project would have looked like RoleNone and lost their drafts. The role is now resolved before the gate, where the answer is needed twice: once to decide who may read a private project, and again to decide who sees drafts on a public one. An anonymous caller costs no extra query, since OptionalUser returns before it touches the database.

The 404/500 matrix was proven unchanged rather than argued: a throwaway probe over {draft, published} × {public, secured, private} × {anonymous, garbage token, stranger, viewer, editor, owner} run against both the old and new handler, byte-identical.

The new tests were checked for teeth by stubbing stripDraftEvents to a no-op — the three guest assertions fail, the member ones stay green.

Verified against production after release, not merely merged: a scratch published project with three Events (draft, published, and one without the field) read back through both public doors with no credentials returns only the published and the legacy one, while the owner still reads all three.

Known residual: an Event photo is an ordinary project file, so it stays listed in uploadedFiles and is fetchable by name from a published project. The flag hides the Event, not its bytes. Closing it needs the stripped events' photo names filtered out of uploadedFiles, or per-file gating.

issues.display_title: Issue #171: feat(project): store a project password (schema + PATCH), hashed and never echoed
issues.main_description_html:
Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

FE PRD: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#946 · Decisions: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#955
Precedent: #168 (project visibility) — same shape, same hazards.

Storage for a project password. No gate yet — that is the sibling task.

Build

Column + migration. Add to Project in src/models/models.go, next to IsPublic:

  • IsSecured bool — not null;default:false
  • PasswordHash string — nullable, json:"-"

Write migrations/<version>_add_secured_to_projects.sql copying the shape of 202609070001_add_is_public_to_projects.sql (-- +migrate Up, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS).

PATCH key. In src/action/v1/project/update.go, add the whitelist entries. Two things the existing pattern does NOT do and this must:

  • Hash before it reaches dbUpdates. The whitelist writes values straight to the DB. Use utils.HashPassword (src/utils/password.go) — bcrypt is already a direct dependency, add nothing.
  • Reject an empty password when isSecured is being turned on. The handler has no validation step at all today; this needs one.

Turning secured off must clear the hash, not leave it lying in the row.

Never echo the hash. projectResponse (src/action/v1/project/shared.go) is returned by Update, Create, List and Recent — adding a field there exposes it on four endpoints at once. Surface is_secured only; never password_hash.

Deploy order — the #940 trap, again

Deploys do not run migrations, and DB_AUTO_MIGRATE is only false on shared/production. The column will appear silently in dev via GORM AutoMigrate and be absent in production. Ship the reading code first and every query touching projects fails — that is the /v1/live 403-for-everyone incident from #940.

ALTER the shared DB (192.168.1.227) before merging to main. Verify the row count afterwards.

Tests

Extend src/routes/v1/project_visibility_test.go's harness (setupRoleMatrix): default is not secured; PATCH sets is_secured + stores a hash that is not the plaintext; PATCH with isSecured:true and an empty password is rejected; turning it off clears the hash; no response body on any of the four endpoints contains the hash.

Blocked on

D1 decides whether this is a third field or a value on a single visibility setting. If D1=B the column shape changes — do not start until it is answered.

RESULT

Implemented on feature/171-project-visibility-secured, merged in #173, released to main in #175 and deployed.

is_public became one setting with three values plus a write-only bcrypt password. PATCH /v1/projects/:id accepts visibility and password, validates the enum explicitly (the whitelist is an untyped map, so a misspelled value would otherwise be written straight to the column and still answer 200), and refuses secured without a password.

visibility deliberately carries no NOT NULL and no default. AutoMigrate runs on every API boot but deploy never runs migrations/, so the column can appear before the backfill — a default of 'public' would have silently opened every private project in that window. issues.display_title: Issue #184: Keep the project password viewable for its owner and editors
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Source: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1098 · FE counterpart: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1099

Problem

Once a project password is set, nobody can see it again. The API keeps it write-only: PATCH /v1/projects/:id stores only a bcrypt hash in projects.password_hash (json:"-", src/action/v1/project/update.go:133). The Share modal can only say "A password is set", so an owner who wants to hand the password to a viewer has to set a new one. #1098 asks for the password to be viewable.

Stored encrypted, not in plain text. Dev reads the production database (the dev BE on 192.168.1.226 uses it), and people reuse passwords. With plain text, anyone with database access or a backup would have every project password.

Scope

  • Unlock doesn't change. password_hash (bcrypt) stays the only thing POST /v1/live/:key/unlock checks. floorplan/unlock.go is untouched.
  • New nullable column projects.password_encrypted (text). The password is encrypted with AES-256-GCM, with a fresh random nonce on every write, and stored as base64(nonce ‖ ciphertext). json:"-" on the model.
  • Key: derived from the existing JWT_SECRET, so there is no new env var. Use HKDF-SHA256 (Go stdlib crypto/hkdf, Go 1.25 here) with info "project-password-v1" and 32 bytes of output. The raw JWT secret is never the AES key itself, so this key stays separate from the HMAC key that signs sessions and project grants.
  • PATCH /v1/projects/:id with password: a non-empty value sets both password_hash and password_encrypted; "" clears both. duplicate.go clears both, as it does for the hash today.
  • New GET /v1/projects/:id/password, with the same gate as GET /:id/embed-grant: owner or editor (CanWrite) only; they can already replace the password and mint an embed grant that skips it.
    • 200 {"password": "<plaintext>"}.
    • 200 {"password": null} when there is nothing to show: the project isn't secured, or its password was set before this change (hash only).
    • 401 without a session, 403 for viewers and non-members, 404 for an unknown project.
    • Cache-Control: no-store.
  • Never elsewhere: password_encrypted and the decrypted value never appear in any other response or in logs.

Deploy

  • Add a migration migrations/202609xx0001_add_password_encrypted_to_projects.sql with ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS.
  • Deploy does not run migrations, and a merge to development already deploys to 1.226. So ALTER the shared database (192.168.1.227) before merging.
  • Ship this before the FE task. The FE falls back to today's behaviour while this endpoint is missing.

Known limits

  • Passwords set before this change exist only as a bcrypt hash and can't be recovered. The owner types it once more to make it viewable.
  • Rotating JWT_SECRET makes stored passwords unreadable. Unlock still works through the hash; owners re-enter. A rotation already signs everyone out and invalidates every grant.

Acceptance criteria

  • After setting a password, GET /v1/projects/:id/password returns it to the owner and to an editor; a viewer or non-member gets 403, no session gets 401.
  • Changing the password returns the new one; clearing it ("") clears both columns and returns null.
  • A project secured before this change returns null, and unlocking it with its password still works.
  • Unlock behaves exactly as before for new and old passwords.
  • A duplicated project has neither column set.
  • password_encrypted is absent from project GET, list and PATCH responses.
  • The stored value differs on every save of the same password (random nonce), and isn't the plaintext.
  • go test ./... passes.

RESULT

PR #185, merge 711746d, commit c61a1f4.

  • src/utils/project_password.go: AES-256-GCM. The key is HKDF-SHA256 over JWT_SECRET (info project-password-v1), with a fresh nonce per write and the project ID bound in as additional data.
  • models.Project.PasswordEncrypted (password_encrypted, json:"-"). PATCH sets the hash and the encrypted copy together, and "" clears both. A duplicate inherits neither. Unlock is unchanged (hash only).
  • GET /v1/projects/:id/password (src/action/v1/project/password.go): CanWrite only, Cache-Control: no-store. Returns {"password": null} when the project isn't secured, the password is hash-only (set before this change), or the stored value no longer decrypts after a JWT_SECRET rotation.
  • Migration 202609240001_add_password_encrypted_to_projects.sql, already applied to 192.168.1.227 before the merge.
  • Tests: src/utils/project_password_test.go (4), src/routes/v1/project_password_test.go (7), and the duplicate test extended. The writer gate is mutation-checked. go test ./... is green.

issues.display_title: Issue #179: perf: GET /v1/floorplan/:id takes 8-53 s for the same project
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Pebi Sandi Pratama — Backend Developer

Frontend counterpart: gothru-3d-floormap#1031. Opening a large project in the editor takes over a minute, and the measurement says the wait is almost entirely one endpoint.

What was measured

Frontend dev server (Next logs the duration of the server action, which is essentially the API call), against the production API at 192.168.1.226:7070, on a scratch copy of Square One Mall V6. Five opens of the same project, nothing else changing:

call endpoint duration
getFloorplanAction GET /v1/floorplan/:id 8.0 s, 16.5 s, 28.3 s, 31.6 s, 52.7 s
getProject GET /v1/projects/:id 0.345 s, 0.378 s, 0.388 s, 0.395 s, 0.398 s

Another project (101be377) came back in 28.3 s and 52.7 s on two consecutive opens.

The response body is about 2.33 MB of JSON, ~677 kB over the wire once compressed.

So: the project row answers in under 0.4 s every time, and the floorplan blob for the same project takes anywhere from 8 to 53 seconds. The frontend cannot show the editor until it arrives.

What this task is

  1. Measure the endpoint server-side — where the time goes inside GET /v1/floorplan/:id: the query, reading the column, JSON handling, the write of last_opened_at if it is on this path, and anything the handler does before it answers.
  2. Explain the spread. A 6× swing on identical input is the interesting part: connection pool waits, a table scan, the row being TOASTed/detoasted, contention with writes from autosave, or something in the storage layer.
  3. Then cut it. Whatever the measurement points at.

Worth checking while you are in there

  • Is the response compressed? 2.33 MB of JSON compresses to roughly a third of that, and the frontend fetches it on every editor open.
  • Does the handler read more than it answers with — e.g. loading the whole project row to return one column?
  • The editor autosaves the same blob every 2 s while someone edits. If reads and writes of that row contend, an open during an active editing session would be the worst case, which matches the spread.

Out of scope

  • The frontend's own handling, which is gothru-3d-floormap#1031.
  • Changing the response shape. The frontend parses this payload as it is; any change to it is a contract change and needs to be agreed there first.

Acceptance criteria

  • A written breakdown of where the time goes inside the endpoint, with numbers.
  • An explanation of why the same request varies by ~6×.
  • A measured improvement on the same project, reported before/after, on the same host.
  • No change to the response shape without agreeing it on gothru-3d-floormap#1031 first.

RESULT

The endpoint is not slow. The 8–53 s in the table above was the network between the machine that measured it and the API. The frontend dev server that logged those numbers reaches 192.168.1.226 through a WireGuard tunnel (toronto-tunnel, 260 ms RTT, pmtu 1420). Production doesn't take that path: its frontend (192.168.1.195) is on the same LAN as the API.

Where the time goes (AC 1)

The same 2.33 MB payload, GET /v1/live/UkZnTKwv, which is built by the same buildFloorplanResponse as /v1/floorplan/:id. Measured with curl -w from the dev machine, 10 runs:

value
TCP connect 0.26 s (1 RTT)
time to first byte 0.79 – 0.85 s, every run
→ server work (TTFB − connect − 1 RTT) ~0.3 s: the project row, the files query, JSON parse and marshal
total 2.7 s – 44 s
→ transfer 1.9 s – 43 s, i.e. the tunnel moving 2.33 MB at 52 – 875 kB/s

The handler buffers the whole response before it writes (c.JSON), so TTFB includes all of the server's work. It stays flat while the total swings 16×.

Payload breakdown: canvasData.levels 1.87 MB (80%), informationRecords 454 kB (19%), everything else < 12 kB. generatedTwin is null here, so nothing is sent twice.

/v1/floorplan/:id itself needs a member token, so it wasn't curled directly. The only extra work on that path is OptionalUser + FetchRoleForProject, two small queries.

Why the same request varies (AC 2)

It's throughput, not the server. TTFB doesn't move while the total does, which rules out pool waits, TOAST, and contention with autosave: all of those would show up before the first byte. The tunnel's throughput is what varies. Three back-to-back runs took 37.7 s, 44.4 s and 33.4 s; five more a minute later took 2.7 – 3.7 s.

For comparison, production seen from a browser (https://map-thru.com/embed/UkZnTKwv, the live server action): 692 kB gzip, TTFB ~1.0 s, done at ~2.2 s.

What changed

The API compressed nothing. cmd/api/main.go registers logger and recover only. Commit 4cc4362 on feature/179-gzip-floorplan-responses adds fiber's own middleware/compress (part of fiber, no new dependency) to exactly two routes, GET /floorplan/:id and GET /live/:key:

  • 2.33 MB → 705 kB on the wire (3.3×), for 46 ms of CPU at LevelBestSpeed. Level 6 would be 698 kB for 104 ms, which is not worth it.
  • Only when the caller sends Accept-Encoding. Node's fetch, which the frontend's server actions use, already sends gzip, deflate and decodes transparently, so the frontend needs no change. A client that sends nothing gets the identical plain body. Response shape unchanged (AC 4).
  • Not app-wide on purpose: fasthttp counts text/event-stream and every application/* type as compressible, so a global middleware would also wrap the SSE streams of /predict, /scan and the storage migration.
  • Test: src/routes/v1/floorplan_gzip_test.go. On both routes it checks: gzip when asked, Vary: Accept-Encoding, body smaller, gunzipped body byte-identical to the plain one, plain JSON when not asked. Mutation-checked: removing the middleware from /live/:key fails it. go test ./... green.

Still open

  • AC 3, the wall-clock before/after on the same host. Deferred to after the deploy, same curl from the same machine. The gain lands where the link is slow: the dev tunnel, and anyone else reading the API over a WAN. The production frontend is on the API's LAN, so its server-side fetch won't change noticeably. What the browser downloads there was already gzipped by Next/Caddy.

Released

  • PR #180 → development (6535dbf), release PR #181 → main (1675054).
  • 192.168.1.226:7070 picked it up from the development merge, before the release PR existed. A request mid-restart was cut off at 287 kB, and the next one already came back Content-Encoding: gzip. So that host tracks development, not only main.
  • Frontend smoke after deploy: https://map-thru.com/embed/UkZnTKwv loads, and clicking a linked unit opens its info card (panelCount: 1). The production frontend decodes the gzipped payload.

AC 3: before/after, same host, same moment

Interleaved from the same dev machine through the same tunnel, alternating plain / Accept-Encoding: gzip, 4 pairs, 150 s cap. The tunnel was in a slow spell (12–18 kB/s), so the absolute numbers are bad for both. The ratio is the result.

pair plain (2.33 MB) gzip (705 kB)
1 timed out at 150 s, 1.76 MB received 41.3 s
2 timed out at 150 s, 1.38 MB received 46.8 s
3 timed out at 150 s, 2.03 MB received 52.9 s
4 108.5 s 38.6 s

Every gzip request completed. 3 of 4 plain ones didn't finish inside 150 s. Where both finished, gzip was 2.8× faster, in line with the 3.3× byte ratio.

TTFB, 6 short pairs: plain 0.78–0.81 s, gzip 0.80–0.84 s. The ~30 ms difference is the compression (46 ms measured offline). Two outliers of ~1.7–1.9 s showed up once in each mode. Both came from time_connect = 1.28 s, a SYN retransmit on the tunnel, not from the server.

issues.display_title: Issue #182: POST /v1/auth/keycloak: exchange a Keycloak access token for a Floormap session
issues.main_description_html:
Backend counterpart to GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1080 (Continue with GoThru). Floormap signs users in through GoThru's central Keycloak (realm gothru); the Go API has to accept that identity and issue its own session token, the same way POST /v1/auth/google does for Google.

Contract source: GoThruMedia/gothru-sso docs/gothru-sso-integration-guide.md — the pattern Panorra already runs (Angular → POST /auth/keycloak → Go backend → Panorra JWT).

⚠️ API contract change: a new public endpoint and a new table.

Endpoint

POST /v1/auth/keycloak — public, registered next to /google in src/routes/v1/auth.go.

  • Request: { "access_token": "<Keycloak access token>" } (the guide's contract; the FE sends nothing else). The FE obtains it with keycloak-js from the public clients floormap-dev / floormap (per the SSO admin, 2026-09-21).
  • Response: same AuthResponse as /v1/auth/google (message, token) — a session token middleware.Auth() accepts. The FE only reads data.token.
  • Errors (the guide's table): 400 missing token · 401 invalid/expired token · 403 local user blocked · 409 account conflict (below) · 502 Keycloak unreachable · 500 anything else.

Token verification

The guide's Option B (JWT/JWKS), with github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5 (already in go.mod; no new dependency):

  • RS256 signature against {KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL}/realms/{KEYCLOAK_REALM}/protocol/openid-connect/certs; cache the keys, refetch once on an unknown kid (key rotation). JWKS unreachable → 502.
  • Pin alg to RS256 (reject none and HS*). Never read claims before the signature passes.
  • iss == {KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL}/realms/{KEYCLOAK_REALM}, exp / nbf with a small leeway, non-empty sub.
  • aud contains KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE = gothru-api (the audience the SSO admin configured on Floormap's clients).
  • azp ∈ KEYCLOAK_ALLOWED_CLIENTS = floormap,floormap-dev. gothru-api is shared by every GoThru app, so azp is what pins the token to Floormap — otherwise another app's token for the same user would open a Floormap session. Both ids are needed because this one backend (192.168.1.226) serves local development (floormap-dev) and production (floormap). The GoThru API's keycloak-login checks azp against an allow-list the same way.

(The guide's Option A — calling /protocol/openid-connect/userinfo — also works, but still needs the aud/azp checks and costs a round trip per login.)

User mapping

Per the guide, a link table keyed on the immutable sub — email and username can change:

user_keycloak_links: user_id (→ users.unique_id, unique) · realm_name · keycloak_sub · keycloak_email · keycloak_username · linked_at, with a unique index on (realm_name, keycloak_sub). (Modelled on gothru-sso/sql/001_create_user_keycloak_link.sql, in this repo's CockroachDB dialect.)

Resolution:

  1. Link with this (realm, sub) → that user.
  2. Otherwise, if email_verified is true and a user has this email → create the link; lift a pending email verification and ClaimInvitations, as GoogleLogin does. Only if product approves (FE #1080 open question 1; the guide says the same).
  3. Otherwise create the user (empty password, EmailVerified from the claim), the link, and ClaimInvitations.

Conflicts → 409, never relink silently:

  • the email's user is already linked to a different sub;
  • the email exists but email_verified is false (creating would collide with the unique email index; linking would be unsafe).

Migration

  • migrations/<date>_create_user_keycloak_links.sql + the model.
  • Deploy order: deploy does not run migrations, and merging to development already deploys to 192.168.1.226 — apply the migration to the shared DB before merging.

Env

  • KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL=https://id.gothru.org (production — discovery live, checked 2026-09-21)
  • KEYCLOAK_REALM=gothru
  • KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE=gothru-api
  • KEYCLOAK_ALLOWED_CLIENTS=floormap,floormap-dev

⚠️ The guide's backend example says KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL=https://auth.gothru.co, but that host is not Keycloak (/realms/gothru/... → 404) and the issuer in production tokens is https://id.gothru.org/realms/gothru. Using auth.gothru.co would fail every issuer check. The guide's dev host https://gothru-sso.web.id answered 502 on 2026-09-21.

Acceptance criteria

  • A valid Keycloak access token from floormap or floormap-dev returns a session token; GET /v1/auth/me works with it.
  • Rejected with 401: wrong iss, aud without gothru-api, azp outside the allow-list (another app's token), expired, bad signature, alg: none (tests against an httptest JWKS server with a generated RSA key).
  • 502 when the JWKS cannot be fetched.
  • Mapping tests: linked sub; verified-email link (if approved); new user; linked-to-another-sub → 409; unverified email colliding with an existing user → 409.
  • Existing /login and /google behave exactly as before.
  • Migration file added and applied to the shared DB before merge.
  • go test ./... green.

RESULT

Merged to development in PR #183 (856d4da, commit a3dca0a) and auto-deployed to 192.168.1.226.

  • POST /v1/auth/keycloak (src/action/v1/auth/keycloak.go, controller, route). The access token is verified locally against the realm JWKS: RS256 only, iss, required exp, aud ∋ gothru-api, azp ∈ floormap,floormap-dev. Keys are cached, with at most one refetch a minute for an unknown kid. Missing config fails closed.
  • user_keycloak_links table + models.UserKeycloakLink. Lookup order: existing link → user with a verified matching email (verification lifted, invitations claimed, like Google) → new user. Relinking is refused (409). A deleted linked user gets 403, an unreachable realm 502.
  • Migration 202609210001 applied to mapthru before merge: 9 columns, 3 indexes, 0 rows (checked).
  • go test ./... and go vet green. 11 forged-token cases are refused with no user created. Mutation checks: removing the azp, aud or email_verified check each turns a test red.

Live check on 192.168.1.226 after deploy:

request result
before merge 404 (route absent)
{} 400 ✅
{"access_token":"not.a.jwt"} 500: KEYCLOAK_* not loaded by the running process (the only 500 before parsing is ErrKeycloakNotConfigured)
/v1/auth/google {} 400 (unchanged)

Pending: add the four KEYCLOAK_* values to the server's .env (read once at start by godotenv) and restart the process. After that, a garbage token must answer 401. An RS256 token with an unknown kid must also answer 401, which proves the server can reach id.gothru.org; if it cannot, the answer is 502.
