issues.display_title: Issue #188: Store the user's GoThru API token at GoThru sign-in and proxy Blue Line reads
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan G�� Developer

Follow-up to #182 (Continue with GoThru). FE counterpart: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1104.

The Blue Line dashboard and editor (PRD GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1082, fixtures only since #1092) now have real read endpoints on the GoThru API (GoThru-API-New, handed over by the GoThru backend team on 2026-09-24). All three authenticate with the user's GoThru API token (gt.<jwt>), and Floormap doesn't have one. This task gets that token when the user signs in with GoThru, stores it encrypted, and exposes the three reads to the FE through this API. The FE never sees the token.

G��n+� API contract change: two new columns on user_keycloak_links and three new authenticated endpoints.

Upstream endpoints

Checked on GoThru API main 92cce80fd; Bruno collection api-collection/GoThru API NEW/User/Tours/.

Endpoint Scope Returns (data)
POST /v1/auth/keycloak-login, body {"token": "<Keycloak access token>"} public token = gt.<jwt>, TTL 30 days (KeycloakLoginAction)
GET /v1/tours/list?page&limit&search&sort_by&type=blueline caller's tours list_tours[] (moderation_id, tour_key, business_name, thumb, total_panorama, place_id, place_address, lat, lng, last_save, publish_status, blueline_error, archived, GǪ) + pagination
GET /v1/panoramas/locations?mid caller's tour (m.user_id) panoramas[] (id, lat/lng as strings, fid, sequence, is_vslide); no limit = all
GET /v2/panoramas/links?mid any valid token (no ownership check) links: [[[lng,lat],[lng,lat]], GǪ] G�� always encrypted
  • The auth header is the raw token: Authorization: gt.<jwt>, with no Bearer. GoThru strips only the gt. prefix.
  • Responses are encrypted unless the request sends the header enc: false (global NormalizeEncryptFlag). /v2/panoramas/links ignores that header; see Decryption.
  • GT tokens are stateless JWTs, revoked through a Redis denylist. Getting one here doesn't sign the user out of other GoThru apps, and a Keycloak logout doesn't revoke it.

Scope

  1. Migration: add gt_token_enc TEXT NULL and gt_token_expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL to user_keycloak_links.
  2. Exchange at sign-in (POST /v1/auth/keycloak, after the user is resolved): send the same Keycloak access token to {GOTHRU_API_BASE}/v1/auth/keycloak-login as {"token": GǪ} (the field is token, not access_token). Take data.token, read exp from its payload, encrypt it, and store it on the link row.
    • Best-effort. Log any failure with the status only, never the token: GoThru down, 401 because floormap isn't an allowed client yet, an account conflict, an inactive GoThru user. The Floormap sign-in still succeeds. Use a short timeout (5 s) so a slow GoThru API can't stall login.
    • Every GoThru sign-in overwrites the stored token, so signing in again is how a user reconnects.
  3. Encryption: AES-256-GCM with a key derived by HKDF from JWT_SECRET. Reuse src/utils/project_password.go (#184) with its own info string, e.g. gothru-gt-token-v1. A value that doesn't decrypt (for example after JWT_SECRET rotates) counts as not connected.
  4. Proxy endpoints behind middleware.Auth(). Each one loads the caller's token from their link row:
    • GET /v1/gothru/tours?page&limit&search&sort_by&type G�� /v1/tours/list
    • GET /v1/gothru/tours/:mid/panoramas G�� /v1/panoramas/locations?mid=
    • GET /v1/gothru/tours/:mid/links G�� /v2/panoramas/links?mid=, decrypted here. GoThru doesn't check who owns the tour on this route, so check first: call /v1/panoramas/locations?mid=&limit=1 (scoped to the caller) and answer 404 when it's empty. Otherwise this proxy would pass the hole through.
    • :mid must be a positive integer. Forward only the listed query params, URL-encoded.
    • Response: GoThru's data object, unchanged, inside this API's usual envelope.
    • Errors:
      • no link, no token, expired or undecryptable G�� 409 gothru_not_connected
      • GoThru answers 401 G�� clear the stored token, then 409 gothru_not_connected
      • GoThru unreachable or 5xx G�� 502
      • any other GoThru 4xx G�� same status

Don't use https://apil.gothru.co: it resolves to the public 208.76.107.71, the same hairpin-NAT setup that broke the JWKS fetch to id.gothru.org (#187). Checked from 192.168.2.15: 1.177 answers all four routes (401/409 without a token). Not checked from 1.226.

Decryption (/v2/panoramas/links)

Preferred: GoThru honours enc on this endpoint the way its v1 siblings do. PanoramasController@getPanoramaLinksV2 calls encryptResult unconditionally; with that fixed, no crypto is needed here. Until then, port HelperClass::encryptResult (app/Class/HelperClass.php:609) in reverse:

  • Split data.ls (e.g. 2026-09-25T10:11:12.123456+07:00) into Y m d H i s. Then formula = ((H*d) XOR 1) + ((i*d) XOR 1) + s*d + int("Ym"). This follows PHP precedence: $hours * $day ^ 3 / 3 is (H*d) ^ (3/3).
  • password = e4[:5] + str(formula) + e4[5:]
  • key = PBKDF2-SHA512(password, salt = hexdecode(su1fur), 999 iterations), first 32 bytes. hash_pbkdf2(..., 64) returns 64 hex characters.
  • AES-256-CBC with iv = hexdecode(f0ur), ciphertext base64decode(c1p), PKCS#7 padding. The result is JSON { "links": GǪ, "messages": GǪ }.
  • Test against a real captured response, not just a round trip through our own port.

Dependencies

  • The GoThru API deployment adds floormap,floormap-dev to KEYCLOAK_ALLOWED_CLIENTS (default app-gothru,gothru-dashboard,app-gothru-local). Without it step 2 always gets 401. Sign-in still works, but the proxies answer 409.

  • Apply the migration to the shared DB before merging to development. Merging deploys to 192.168.1.226, and deploy runs no migrations.
  • Add GOTHRU_API_BASE to the server .env, then restart.

Out of scope

  • Writing panorama positions. The GoThru API has no endpoint for it (PRD R28 is still blocked).
  • A separate "connect" endpoint for users who signed up with email/password. Signing in once with GoThru links their account (verified-email match, #182).
  • Keycloak refresh tokens. They aren't stored: the GT token lives 30 days, and after that the user signs in with GoThru again.

Acceptance criteria

  • A GoThru sign-in stores an encrypted GT token and its expiry on the link row. The DB never holds it in plaintext and logs never print it.
  • A GoThru API failure during sign-in still returns a Floormap session.
  • The three proxies return GoThru's data for the caller's own tours, and links come back decrypted.
  • Links for a tour the caller doesn't own G�� 404.
  • No token, expired or undecryptable G�� 409 gothru_not_connected. An upstream 401 clears the token.
  • A non-numeric :mid G�� 400, and nothing is sent upstream.
  • Tests run against an httptest GoThru stub: exchange succeeds, exchange fails, a 401 clears the token, and a real captured /v2/panoramas/links response decrypts.
  • go test ./... green.

Implemented and merged. development at b89c5e5: go build ./..., go vet ./... and go test ./... all pass.

  • Exchange at sign-in: gothru.Connect (src/action/v1/gothru/token.go) is called from src/action/v1/auth/keycloak.go after the user is resolved.
    • It sends the Keycloak access token to {GOTHRU_API_BASE}/v1/auth/keycloak-login with a 5 s timeout, and reads exp from the unverified GT JWT.
    • It is best-effort: a failure is logged without the token, and the sign-in still succeeds. If GOTHRU_API_BASE is unset, it does nothing.
  • Encryption: src/utils/gothru_token.go uses AES-GCM with an HKDF key from JWT_SECRET (info gothru-gt-token-v1, bound to the user), and reuses the #184 helpers.
  • Proxies (src/action/v1/gothru/proxy.go, src/routes/v1/gothru.go, behind middleware.Auth()):

    • GET /v1/gothru/tours/:mid/panoramas G�� /v1/panoramas/locations

issues.display_title: Issue #198: Blue Line save: take the tour key from GoThru, not from the request
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan G�� Developer

Follow-up to #195 (PR #196). Found while checking PRD GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1082 against the released code.

Problem

PUT /v1/gothru/tours/:mid/panoramas (UpdatePanoramas, src/action/v1/gothru/proxy.go) checks that the caller owns :mid, then forwards the request body unchanged to GoThru PUT /v1/internal/panoramas/locations/batch with the Internal-API-Key.

GoThru does not use :mid there. BatchUpdatePanoLocationAction resolves the tour from the body's tour_key (getModerationIdByTourKey) and updates 2_lat / 3_lng of the panoramas of that moderation. The internal endpoint has no user, so it cannot check ownership itself.

:mid and tour_key are never compared. A signed-in user who owns any tour can send their own :mid with another tour's tour_key and overwrite that tour's panorama positions. Tour keys are public (https://tourmkr.com/F1{tour_key}), and so are panorama ids (the public panoramas API).

Checked on this repo main 0084e84 and GoThru API main c165c705b. Both editors that save (single tour, and the multiple-tour editor since gothru-3d-floormap#1142) go through this endpoint.

Scope

Take the tour key from GoThru, not from the request.

  1. Replace the ownership read (/v1/panoramas/locations?mid=&limit=1) with one call to the caller's own tour list, made with the caller's GoThru token: GET /v1/tours/list?search=<tour_key from the body>&limit=100. GoThru scopes that list to the caller (user_id) and search matches tour_key.
  2. Find the row whose moderation_id equals :mid. No such row, or a row with an empty tour_key G�� 404 tour not found, and the internal endpoint is not called.
  3. Forward that row's tour_key to the internal endpoint, with the request's locations. The body's tour_key is a search term only.

The number of GoThru calls stays the same: one read, one write.

Not changing

  • API contract: request and response stay as they are (tour_key is still required in the body). No FE change.
  • GoThru API: no change needed.

Acceptance criteria

  • A request with the caller's :mid and another tour's tour_key answers 404 and never reaches /v1/internal/panoramas/locations/batch.
  • A request with the caller's :mid and its own tour_key is forwarded as before.
  • When the search also matches the :mid row for another reason (search is a LIKE over the name too), the forwarded tour_key is the one GoThru lists for :mid, never the body's.
  • A :mid the caller does not own answers 404, as today.
  • Not connected G�� 409 gothru_not_connected; GoThru down G�� 502; both as today.
  • go test ./... passes.

Known limits

  • limit=100: a search that matches more than 100 of the caller's tours can leave the :mid row off the page, and the save answers 404. It refuses; it never writes to the wrong tour.
  • GoThru lists tour_key from 0_moderation, while the internal endpoint looks in hosted_tours.tours first. GoThru writes the same key to both when it creates a hosted tour (addTourData, GetDetailTourMergeAction), so they agree.

RESULT

Implemented and merged to development (8a18148, PR #199). go build ./..., go vet ./... and go test ./... pass.

What changed (src/action/v1/gothru/proxy.go)

  • New ownTourKey(userID, mid, hint): one read of the caller's own tour list with the caller's GoThru token (GET /v1/tours/list?search=<tour_key from the body>&limit=100). It returns the tour_key of the row whose moderation_id equals :mid.
  • UpdatePanoramas forwards that key to PUT /v1/internal/panoramas/locations/batch. The body's tour_key is a search term only. No row for :mid, or a row without a key G�� 404 tour not found, and the internal endpoint is not called.
  • This replaces the earlier ownership read (/v1/panoramas/locations?mid=&limit=1): still one GoThru read and one write. The API contract is unchanged, so the FE needs nothing.

Tests (src/action/v1/gothru/proxy_test.go)

  • Another tour's key with the caller's :mid G�� 404, no batch call.
  • A :mid the caller does not own G�� 404, no batch call.
  • The :mid row found through its name G�� the forwarded key is GoThru's, not the body's.
  • A tour without a key G�� 404. Not connected G�� 409, GoThru not called.
  • Mutation checks: forwarding the body's key, and accepting any listed row, each turn a test red.

Not verified: the fix was not run against the live GoThru API. It relies on the deployed tour list matching tour_key in search (in GoThru's searchModerationIds since 2026-05-07). A 404 on every Blue Line save after deploy would mean the deployed search differs.

Known limit: limit=100. A search matching more than 100 of the caller's tours can miss the :mid row; the save then answers 404 and writes nothing.

Released to main (250db6a, PR #200).

issues.display_title: Issue #201: Connect, show and disconnect a GoThru account for the signed-in user
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan G�� Developer

Bug report: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1107. PM decisions: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1151. Follow-up to #182 and #188.

Problem

On the Blue Line page, Connect to GoThru Dashboard runs the same flow as Continue with GoThru on the login page: the FE posts the Keycloak access token to POST /v1/auth/keycloak, which is public and resolves the Floormap user from the GoThru identity (link by sub, then verified email, then a new user). It never knows who is signed in, so the answer is a session for that user and the signed-in account is replaced. In #1107 a tester signed in with Google as one account and ended up in another.

There is no way to attach a GoThru account to the account that is already signed in, to see which one is attached, or to detach it.

Decisions (#1151)

  1. Connect attaches the GoThru account to the signed-in Floormap account. Name, email, projects and role do not change.
  2. A GoThru account already attached to another Floormap account is refused.
  3. The Blue Line page shows which GoThru account is connected (its email).
  4. A Disconnect action. To use another GoThru account, the user disconnects and connects again. Nothing is removed in GoThru.
  5. A GoThru email that differs from the Floormap email is allowed.

POST /v1/auth/keycloak (sign-in) stays as it is.

Scope

G��n+� API contract change: three new endpoints under /v1/gothru, behind middleware.Auth(). No migration: user_keycloak_links already holds everything.

GET /v1/gothru/connection

G�� 200 { "connected": bool, "email": string }

  • connected: the caller has a usable GoThru token (the same rule the tour proxies use before answering 409 gothru_not_connected).
  • email: the linked GoThru account's email (its username when Keycloak sent no email), "" when there is no link.

POST /v1/gothru/connection, body { "access_token": "<Keycloak access token>" }

Verifies the token exactly as POST /v1/auth/keycloak does (signature, issuer, audience, azp), then:

  • (realm, sub) linked to the caller G�� refresh the GoThru token.
  • (realm, sub) linked to another user G�� 409 gothru_account_in_use. Nothing changes.
  • the caller is linked to a different sub G�� 409 gothru_already_connected (disconnect first).
  • otherwise G�� create the link for the caller.

Then trade the token for the GoThru API token (gothru.Connect). Unlike at sign-in, this is not best-effort: a failed exchange answers 502 and a link created by this request is removed, so a connect either works or leaves nothing behind.

G�� 200 { "connected": true, "email": "GǪ" }

Other errors: 400 missing access_token, 400 invalid GoThru token (not the 401 the sign-in answers: behind a session, 401 means the Floormap session is gone), 502 Keycloak keys unreachable.

No email rule applies here (decision 5): the caller is already signed in to Floormap and the token proves they hold the GoThru account.

DELETE /v1/gothru/connection

Deletes the caller's link row, and the stored GoThru token with it. G�� 200 { "connected": false, "email": "" }. Idempotent.

  • 409 gothru_sign_in_only when the caller has no password and an unverified email: GoThru is the only way into that account, and without the link the next GoThru sign-in would be refused (the email branch of resolveKeycloakUser needs a verified email).
  • The GoThru account is free afterwards: it can be connected to another Floormap account, or used to sign in.

Behaviour to know

  • A user who signs in with Continue with GoThru is connected again by that sign-in (it creates the link and stores the token, as today). Disconnect lasts until they next sign in with GoThru.
  • User has no marker for Google sign-in, so a user without a password cannot be told apart further than the rule above. A GoThru-created user with a verified email who disconnects is linked again by email at the next GoThru sign-in.

Acceptance criteria

  • Connect with a GoThru account that is not linked: the caller gets the link and the token; the caller's name, email and role are unchanged; no session is issued.
  • Connect with a GoThru account linked to another user G�� 409 gothru_account_in_use; neither user's link changes.

issues.display_title: Issue #219: Clean up leftovers from upload content sniffing (#80)
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Clean Up Leftovers from Upload Content Sniffing (Issue #219)

Overview

This task performs architectural clean-up following the upload content sniffing hardening implemented in Issue #80 (PR #216) and subsequent response sanitization in Issue #81 (PR #217). It removes obsolete helper functions, redundant validation maps, and unreachable code branches, formats test suites to ensure gofmt compliance, and adds the X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff security header across all API responses.

Motivation & Background

In Issue #80, file upload validation was transitioned from trusting client-supplied multipart headers (Content-Type) and client file extensions to server-side magic byte inspection via shared.DetectImageUpload.

This left behind:

  1. Two side-by-side validators (AllowedImageUpload and DetectImageUpload), causing ambiguity regarding the canonical upload gate.
  2. Deprecated helper functions and struct maps with zero production callers (helpers.AvatarExt, shared.CanonicalExtFromMime, shared.AllowedMime, shared.allowedExts, shared.allowedMimes, and normalizeContentType).
  3. An unneeded package dependency from src/helpers to src/action/v1/shared.
  4. Unreachable fallback branches for SVG attachments in file-serving endpoints.
  5. Missing X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff response headers, which prevent browsers from MIME-sniffing a polyglot response away from the server-declared Content-Type.

Code Implementation Details

1. Formatting (src/action/v1/shared/upload_validation_test.go)

  • Aligned test case struct fields and map definitions to comply strictly with standard Go formatting rules.
  • Verified that gofmt -l ./src passes with zero formatting diffs.

2. Dead Code Removal

  • src/helpers/avatar.go & src/helpers/avatar_test.go:
    • Deleted both files. helpers.AvatarExt previously fell back to client-supplied extensions. With upload extensions strictly derived from detected MIME types in DetectImageUpload, this helper was obsolete. Deleting it completely removed the coupling between src/helpers and src/action/v1/shared.
  • shared.CanonicalExtFromMime & shared.AllowedImageUpload (src/action/v1/shared/shared.go):
    • Removed shared.CanonicalExtFromMime as no callers remained.
    • Removed shared.AllowedImageUpload. Refactored existing test suites (upload_validation_test.go) to test DetectImageUpload directly.
  • normalizeContentType (src/action/v1/auth/update_profile.go):
    • Removed the unused private helper function from the profile update action layer.
  • Validation Map Consolidation (src/action/v1/shared/shared.go):
    • Removed allowedExts, allowedMimes, and the helper function AllowedMime.
    • Consolidated validation in DetectImageUpload to check directly against mimeToCanonicalExt. If the detected MIME is absent from mimeToCanonicalExt, it is rejected as ErrUnsupportedFileType.

3. Removal of Unreachable SVG Branches

  • In src/action/v1/files/get.go, src/action/v1/files/shared.go (sendProjectFile), and src/controllers/v1/auth/avatar.go:
    • Removed the if ext == ".svg" || mimeType == "image/svg+xml" blocks setting Content-Disposition: attachment.
    • Content types for serving endpoints derive from MimeTypeFromExt, which does not contain .svg and falls back to application/octet-stream. Additionally, SVG uploads are rejected at ingestion, rendering these inline SVG handling blocks unreachable.

4. Global X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff Header

  • cmd/api/main.go:
    • Added global Fiber middleware before route registration: 
      app.Use(func(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
    c.Set("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
    return c.Next()
})
    • Refactored server bootstrapping into buildApp() *fiber.App to enable programmatic testing.
  • cmd/api/main_test.go:
    • Added unit test TestNosniffResponseHeader asserting that all responses from buildApp() carry X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
  • src/routes/v1/upload_hardening_test.go:
    • Added assertions confirming that authenticated upload responses (both project file and avatar) deliver X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

Security & Architectural Impact

  • MIME Confusion & Polyglot Defense: The X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header instructs browsers to strictly respect the server-declared Content-Type. If an attacker constructs an image/HTML polyglot file, browsers will not re-sniff or execute it as HTML/JavaScript.
  • Single Source of Truth: shared.DetectImageUpload is now the single, unambiguous gate for all upload validation in the application.
  • Clean Dependency Graph: Eradicated cross-layer coupling from helper packages back into business action packages.

Verification & Acceptance Criteria

  • gofmt -l ./src: Clean, zero formatting discrepancies.
  • Dead Code Cleanup: helpers.AvatarExt, shared.CanonicalExtFromMime, shared.AllowedImageUpload, normalizeContentType, allowedExts, allowedMimes, and AllowedMime completely removed.
  • Compilation: go build ./... and go vet ./... succeed with zero errors and warnings.
  • Upload Behavior: Genuine PNG, JPEG, and WebP uploads succeed; non-image and spoofed payloads are rejected with HTTP 400 (src/routes/v1/upload_hardening_test.go passes).
  • Security Header: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff is verified across route and application tests (cmd/api/main_test.go and src/routes/v1/upload_hardening_test.go pass).
  • Full Test Suite: All packages pass via go test ./....

Assignee: Pebi Sandi Pratama G�� Developer

Description

PR #216 (#80) moved upload validation to shared.DetectImageUpload. It shipped with a gofmt failure, helpers that nothing calls any more, and SVG branches that can never run. Clean them up in one PR. Nothing changes for clients except one new response header.

  1. gofmt: src/action/v1/shared/upload_validation_test.go is not gofmt-clean (struct field and map alignment). Run gofmt -w.
